title: The Beacon Fires

source.book: Records of the Grand Historian, Annals of Zhou
source.chapter: written by Sima Qian (Western Han); later scholars doubt the beacon story
source.quote: Bao Si did not like to laugh, and though King You tried every means to make her laugh, she would not. The king had beacon fires and great drums, so that when an enemy came the fires would be lit. The lords all came, and when they arrived there was no enemy, and Bao Si laughed aloud... After that they did not believe it, and the lords came no more.

moral: The fire was real; only the cry of "the enemy" was false — trust runs out.

story.title: The Beacon Towers
story.text: Beacon towers ran along the ridge: light them, and the lords would ride to save the king.
story.narration: Along the western ridge stood one beacon tower after another. When an enemy came, the fires were lit, and the lords far away saw the light and rode to save the king.

story.title: The Queen Who Never Smiled
story.text: King You had a queen named Bao Si who never smiled. One day he lit the fires.
story.narration: King You of Zhou had a queen named Bao Si. She never smiled. One day, to make her laugh, he lit the beacon fires when there was no enemy at all.

keyMoment.question: There is no enemy — what happens if the fires are lit?

options.text: The lords ride over, and find no enemy at the gate
They go and fight the enemy

keyMoment.reveal: Beacon fires are for enemies. Play with them once and it is funny; afterwards no one comes.

misconceptions: Bao Si’s smile destroyed the Western Zhou — the fault was his who lit the fires
Once or twice does not matter

quiz.question: What are the beacon fires for?
options: To call the lords when an enemy comes
To light the road for travellers
quiz.explanation: A beacon is an alarm: when the lords see the fire, they know the king is in danger.

quiz.question: Why did the lords stop coming?
options: They had been tricked several times and no longer believed the fires
They were angry and would not fight
quiz.explanation: The fire shouted "enemy!" again and again, and there was never anyone there — so no one believed it any more.

quiz.question: Which of these is most like the beacon fires?
options: Shouting "Fire!" as a joke, so no one believes you when there is a real fire
Returning what you borrowed on time
quiz.explanation: Lie for fun and people stop trusting you — trust runs out a little at a time.

lines.first: They came — and there was no enemy at the gate.
lines.again: Again they came. Going home, heads shook.
lines.empty: This time they did not even reach the gate.
lines.end: The fire was real; only the alarm was false.
